name: Mir-Hossein Mousavi
role: Prime Minister of Iran (1981-1989), leader of the Green Movement after the 2009 election
summary: Mousavi, prime minister during the Iran-Iraq war and the 2009 reformist presidential candidate, became leader of the Green Movement, demanding full enactment of the Islamic Republic's constitution, freedom of the press, release of political prisoners and accountability for the repression, while insisting on peaceful, legal protest and defending the poor and both workers and employers.

sources.title: Mousavi's Statement #17 Regarding the Events of Bloody Ashura, 1 January 2010 (Persian 11 Dey 1389), Iran Data Portal, Princeton University (translation by Khordaad88)
sources.author: Mir-Hossein Mousavi
sources.usedFor: His five-stage proposal after Ashura 2009: responsibility of government and judiciary, a transparent election law, release of political prisoners, freedom of the press and media, the right to legal demonstrations.

sources.title: The Green Movement Is Standing Firm on Its Rightful Demands, interview, 27 February 2010 (Persian 8 Esfand 1388), Iran Data Portal, Princeton University (translation by Khordaad88)
sources.author: Mir-Hossein Mousavi
sources.usedFor: The movement works peacefully and lawfully through the streets and other legal means; security forces are brothers forced to yield to violence.

sources.title: Mousavi: We should resist until all the issues and problems are resolved, 8 April 2010, Iran Data Portal, Princeton University (translation by Khordaad88)
sources.author: Mir-Hossein Mousavi
sources.usedFor: Free activity for labour, social groups and media as the least costly way to govern; the movement defends workers and employers together and especially the poor.

sources.title: Mousavi's statement of 28 September 2010 on Quds Day and the Islamic Republic, Iran Data Portal, Princeton University (translation by Khordaad88)
sources.author: Mir-Hossein Mousavi
sources.usedFor: Demand for the unconditional enactment of the constitution and the Islamic Republic 'not a word more and not a word less'.

sources.title: Mousavi-Ahmadinejad presidential debate, 3 June 2009, unofficial English transcript from the dubbed video, Critical Threats (American Enterprise Institute)
sources.author: Mir-Hossein Mousavi and Mahmoud Ahmadinejad
sources.usedFor: His criticism of the previous government for shutting nuclear installations and accepting the additional protocol without parliamentary ratification.

sources.title: Mousavi's 'To save Iran' statement of 4 February 2023, as reported by Iran International (Kaleme original)
sources.author: Mir-Hossein Mousavi, reported by Iran International
sources.usedFor: His call for fundamental change, a free referendum on a new constitution and a constituent assembly.

sources.title: Iran policy change behind Cabinet crisis. Bow to free market comes at expense of economic reform, Christian Science Monitor, 16 September 1988
sources.author: Christian Science Monitor
sources.usedFor: His 1988 government's state-interventionist economy, the state-owned foreign trade companies and his struggle over land reform with the free-market clerics and bazaar.

sources.title: Blood-soaked secrets: Why Iran's 1988 prison massacres are ongoing crimes against humanity, Amnesty International (December 2018), PDF copy
sources.author: Amnesty International
sources.usedFor: The 1988 mass prisoner killings under his government and his later claim that they took place without his knowledge.

sources.title: Mir-Hossein Mousavi, Wikipedia
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Orientation to his career as prime minister (1981-89) and the 2009 Green Movement, used to locate the primary texts.
